items.title: New Jersey Takes Kalshi to the Supreme Court
points: New Jersey filed a complaint at the U.S. Supreme Court against Kalshi, a prediction market platform offering contracts tied to real-world events like election outcomes and economic data releases.
The state argues Kalshi operates without required state authorization and violates gambling laws by allowing users to place bets on event outcomes.

Kalshi contends it operates under federal Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) authority, which regulates derivatives (financial contracts whose value depends on underlying assets or events), claiming state gambling laws don't apply.
The dispute reflects a fundamental tension over whether prediction markets fall under federal derivatives regulation or state gambling oversight.
Multiple states have challenged the CFTC's approval of Kalshi's contracts, arguing the platform resembles illegal betting rather than legitimate financial instruments.
Resolution could determine whether prediction markets can expand nationally or remain restricted to limited jurisdictions.

items.title: Wall Street Banks Enter Stablecoin Market
points: Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and other major US banks are forming a consortium to jointly issue a dollar-backed stablecoin (a digital currency pegged 1:1 to the dollar), targeting a 2027 launch.
The collaborative model distributes infrastructure costs and regulatory compliance across members rather than each bank building separate competing products.

The move puts banks in direct competition with USDT and USDC, which dominate global dollar stablecoin supply, reflecting institutional momentum as US federal stablecoin legislation clarifies issuer requirements.

items.title: Argentina's Stablecoin Adoption: From Crisis Hedge to Financial Norm
points: 94% of peso crypto trading routes to stablecoins (the highest share globally), driven by a 2001 banking crisis where the government froze deposits and converted dollar accounts to pesos at a 75% loss.

After 2019 capital controls capped official dollar purchases at $200/month, stablecoins became essential for dollar access; 1 in 5 Argentines now use crypto, with downloads of top 15 crypto apps up 93% in 2024.

Even after Argentina lifted most capital controls in April 2025, narrowing the official-to-parallel exchange rate gap from ~27% to ~4%, users kept downloading stablecoin wallets and maintained USDC payroll allocations, showing a shift from emergency tool to structural financial preference.

items.title: New DeFi and Fintech Yield Products Launch
points: 3Jane's 'levered callable capital' product lets users earn 20%+ APY by staking $75K as margin while keeping up to $1M in additional capital usable elsewhere until called (9-day funding window if called, 35-day cooldown after), positioned as a market for balance-sheet capacity itself.

EthenaPay, a crypto neobank on Avalanche, pairs traditional IBAN bank accounts with self-custodial stablecoin holdings, offering a 6% savings rate, 5% card cashback, free onramps in USD/GBP/EUR/local currencies, and borderless instant transfers via an iOS app.

Privy launched native fiat on/off-ramp orchestration APIs letting developers move funds between bank accounts and stablecoins/wallets, while Ethena Pay's auto-yield routing automatically covers card balances, bringing yield infrastructure directly to consumer fintech.

items.title: Regulatory and Market Friction Points
points: Robinhood Wallet and Fomo allow meme coin purchases via Visa/Mastercard/Apple Pay/Google Pay through Crossmint, which classifies transactions as 'digital goods/media' rather than crypto to bypass credit card network restrictions; Chase flagged the incorrect classification and the NY Attorney General is reviewing.

B2B stablecoin payments totaled only ~$390B in 2025 with ~$226B in B2B volume, dominated by USDT and driven by small/mid-sized importers in Asia; MiCA (EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation) forces corridors to route around USDT, leaving white space in Africa payouts, intra-LATAM, Turkey/CEE, and mid-market Asia.
Kalshi and Polymarket combined monthly volume fell 14.5% to $45.33B in August, marking the first decline in a year after a World Cup-driven summer spike.

items.title: Token Market Moves
points: Arbitrum (ARB) jumped 25% to $0.1087 as Robinhood Chain daily fees doubled to $2.13M, generating ~$192K daily for Arbitrum DAO's 10% licensing cut; Chain DEX volume rose 89.5% weekly to $1.56B with TVL reaching $738.5M, though memecoin speculation drives most activity.
ARB remains 95.5% below its January 2024 peak of $2.39, placing market cap at ~$726M despite weekly gains; Bitcoin held near $78K and total crypto market cap stood at $2.72 trillion.
Strategy's CEO defended buying Bitcoin near $80K after selling at $60K-$65K, arguing capital costs (not price predictions) drove both moves, while the firm grew its Bitcoin holdings 30% this year.
